paper_metadata.title: Optimal Tuning of Quantum Generative Adversarial Networks for Multivariate Distribution Loading

summary: This paper studies a gate-based qGAN for approximate data loading of a discretized lognormal distribution using a layered RY-cZ ansatz on 3 and 4 qubits. The best reported 3-qubit result reaches KS = 0.0296 and relative entropy = 0.0082, improving on prior qGAN benchmarks of KS = 0.0522 (best prior initialization) and 0.0821 (random initialization), while SPSA converges faster but degrades accuracy to around p ≈ 0.1 or worse.

experiments.description: qGAN training for loading a univariate lognormal distribution (used as a proxy for multivariate loading via the discriminator design), evaluated on 3-qubit and 4-qubit cases with Adam AMSGRAD and SPSA hyperparameter sweeps.

algorithm.variant: quantum generative adversarial network (qGAN) with layered RY-cZ ansatz
algorithm.ansatz: layered circuit with initial RY layer followed by k repetitions of cZ entanglement layer and RY rotation layer
algorithm.convergence_criteria: run converges when generator parameters are substantially stable for m = M/200 subsequent epochs; training capped at max epochs per test set
algorithm.parameter_initialization: random initialization of generator and discriminator parameters; multiple random seeds/runs

problem_formulation.encoding_details: generator outputs amplitudes x_i whose squared magnitudes encode approximate probabilities over 2^n bins; discriminator input uses qubit-wise binary representation of samples
problem_formulation.objective_function: non-saturating GAN loss; generator minimizes discriminator’s ability to distinguish generated from target samples

problem_instance.description: Approximate loading of a discretized lognormal distribution for data loading / distribution learning; multivariate capability discussed via discriminator design, but experiments reported on lognormal target distribution

dataset_specification.description: lognormal with mu=1, sigma=1, discretized into 2^n bins on [0,8]

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: 20,000 samples generated; tails trimmed after binning leaving about 17,200 samples; training set shuffled and split into batches of 2000
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 10 independent runs per test case; convergence rate, epochs to convergence, chi-square goodness-of-fit p-values, Kolmogorov-Smirnov statistic, and relative entropy reported; best-run and average-over-converging-runs summaries

noise_model.noise_type: noiseless simulator used for training; statevector simulator used for final evaluation

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: lognormal sampling, binning, trimming tails, batching
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: chi-square test for goodness of fit; Kolmogorov-Smirnov statistic and relative entropy for comparison with prior work

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: best runs show an elbow near convergence; sub-optimal runs show slow, oscillatory, or residual dynamics

speedup_claims.factor: 43% reduction in Kolmogorov-Smirnov statistic vs best prior case; 64% reduction vs similar prior case
speedup_claims.conditions: 3-qubit lognormal target distribution, k=1, Adam AMSGRAD, discriminator size (8,8), 10 runs
speedup_claims.caveats: This is an accuracy improvement, not a computational speedup. Results are specific to the chosen ansatz, simulator, and hyperparameters.

speedup_claims.factor: average performance as low as 36% of benchmark KS; 25% for best choice (32,16)
speedup_claims.conditions: 3-qubit Adam experiments, comparison against Table I in prior work
speedup_claims.caveats: Again, this is a quality improvement metric rather than runtime speedup.

speedup_claims.baseline_method: classical data loading / classical GAN training
speedup_claims.conditions: paper states asymptotic study would require scaling assumptions not available from the small-n experiments
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper explicitly says no speedup order is proven; SPSA may reduce quantum evaluations but at unacceptable accuracy.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: loading cost O(n(k+1)+1); training cost proportional to j·b·(cq_gen_train + cq_discr_train) with cq_gen_train scaling linearly in n(k+1) for Adam and constant in number of evaluations for SPSA
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: training discriminator cost scales with nH1 + H1H2 + H2; overall classical training cost j·b·(cc_gen_train + cc_discr_train)

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: No practical quantum advantage resources demonstrated; experiments are on noiseless/statevector simulators with 3- and 4-qubit circuits and a classical discriminator. The paper reports improved approximation quality over a prior qGAN baseline, not over a strong classical end-to-end solver.
limiting_factors: No QPU execution; only noiseless and statevector simulators
Problem sizes are toy-scale (3 and 4 qubits)
Classical discriminator dominates part of the workflow
SPSA is faster but much less accurate
No end-to-end classical baseline for the same task is shown to be beaten

notes: Hardware inferred as simulator_other because the paper explicitly says training was carried on the noiseless simulator and final evaluation on the statevector simulator; no real QPU device is named.
The paper reports both 3-qubit and 4-qubit experiments; the main benchmark/tuning discussion centers on 3 qubits, with appendix results for 4 qubits.
No gate counts, transpiled depth, or fidelity metrics are reported.
The paper claims improved qGAN training quality versus prior qGAN work, not a demonstrated practical quantum advantage over classical methods.
The reported setting is NISQ-style simulation, so Hoefler viability is not supported.
